---
title: "3 · Haar Measure & Weingarten Calculus"
---

This is the technical heart of the tutorial. The **Haar measure** is the unique
uniform distribution over the unitary group, and almost every quantitative result
in later chapters is a *low moment* of it — an average of one or two copies of a
random unitary acting on an operator.

The **Weingarten calculus** is the machine that evaluates those averages. The idea
is simple once you see it: averaging $k$ copies of $U$ projects onto the operators
that commute with $U^{\otimes k}$, and by Schur–Weyl duality those are exactly the
**permutations** of the copies. An integral over a continuous group collapses to a
finite sum over the symmetric group, weighted by Weingarten functions.

With this you can compute, by hand, things that look hard:

- the **first moment** (twirling) — any operator averages to its trace times the
  identity;
- the **second moment** — purities, frame potentials, and the **Page formula**
  for the entanglement of a typical state;
- **concentration of measure** — why those averages are not just typical but
  *overwhelmingly* so as the dimension grows.

These three facts power Chapters 5–7. Do this chapter carefully.

## Notebooks in this part

- [The first Haar moment (twirling)](../notebooks/ch3/solution_ch3_weingarten_first_moment.ipynb) — averaging an operator to its trace times the identity.
- [The SWAP trick](../notebooks/ch3/solution_ch3_swap_trick.ipynb) — turning purity into a two-copy expectation value.
- [Overlaps of random states](../notebooks/ch3/solution_ch3_haar_overlap.ipynb) — the distribution of $|\langle\psi|\phi\rangle|^2$ and its moments.
- [Fourth moment of the trace](../notebooks/ch3/solution_ch3_fourth_moment_trace.ipynb) — a warm-up: $\mathbb{E}|\mathrm{Tr}\,U|^4 = 2$.
- [Weingarten calculus as tensor networks](../notebooks/ch3/solution_ch3_tensor_weingarten_calculus.ipynb) — diagrammatic contractions, including the third trace moment.
- [The Page formula](../notebooks/ch3/solution_ch3_page_formula.ipynb) — average entanglement of a random state, via Marchenko–Pastur.
- [Concentration of purity](../notebooks/ch3/solution_ch3_purity_concentration.ipynb) — why a random subsystem is almost exactly maximally mixed.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
The single most reused result in this tutorial is the **second-moment twirl**
$\mathbb{E}_U[U^{\otimes 2}\,X\,U^{\dagger\otimes 2}] = c_{\mathbb{I}}\,\mathbb{I} + c_{\mathbb{F}}\,\mathbb{F}$.
If you internalize one calculation, make it this one.
:::
